# Your first interface, in C++

The three files under `res/` are on [the previous page](README.md); the `CMakeLists.txt`
is [a C++ project](../adding-to-a-project/cpp.md). This is the one file left.

## `main.cpp`

```cpp
#include <RendeerAlpha.h>
#include <Layout/LayoutHost.h>
#include <RdaState.h>            // generated by rda_add_state

#include <iostream>

namespace {
    RDA::Layout::LayoutHost gHost;

    // A development build watches the layout's source, so editing it rebuilds the
    // interface in place. A release build has no source to watch.
    std::string sourceDir() {
#ifdef MYAPP_SOURCE_DIR
        return std::string(MYAPP_SOURCE_DIR) + "/res/layouts";
#else
        return {};
#endif
    }
}

int main() {
    RDA::AppConfig config;
    config.app.name = "My application";
    config.gui.themePath = "res/themes/app.rdth";

    config.onStart = [] {
        // The names first. A binding resolves what it reads when it is created, and
        // one that does not exist yet is guessed at rather than found.
        RDA::State::define();

        // What commands.save() does.
        RDA::State::onSave([] {
            std::cout << "saving: " << RDA::State::notes() << "\n";
        });

        gHost.open(getMainWindow()->gui().retained(),
                   "res/layouts/home.rdab", sourceDir() + "/home.tsx");
    };

    // Reloading restructures the widget tree, so it happens here rather than inside a
    // widget callback -- a callback fires while that tree is being walked.
    config.onUpdate = [](float) { gHost.reloadIfChanged(); };

    rendeerRun(config);
}
```

Everything typed comes from `RdaState.h`, which the build generated from `res/state.ts`:
`RDA::State::count()`, `setCount()`, `notes()`, `onSave()`. Rename `save` in the
declaration and this file stops compiling, which is the point.

`rendeerRun` blocks until the window closes. The engine owns the window and the loop; the
callbacks are your program. A program that already has a main loop runs it `Owned` instead
— see [an application that already exists](../adding-to-a-project/existing-application.md).

## Run it

```bash
cmake -B build
cmake --build build --config Debug
cd build/bin/Debug && ./myapp
```

From that directory, because assets resolve relative to the working directory. Started
from anywhere else it stops at once with a message saying the font could not be loaded.

Press *Save* and the console prints whatever is in the field. Edit `home.tsx` while it
runs, and the interface follows.

## From here

- More than one screen: [screens](../../frontend/screens.md), and a `Router` in place of
  the `LayoutHost` — [the C++ backend](../../backend/cpp.md) shows both.
- Rows from data: declare a table in `state.ts`, fill it from C++, show it with
  [`<list>`](../../frontend/elements/list.md).
- Check it without a window: [testing what you build](../testing.md).
